texts.preamble: Khaleel Ahmad vs State Of U.P. on 17 May, 2024 Author: Samit Gopal Bench: Samit Gopal High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:89699 Court No. - 87 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2784 of 2012 Revisionist :- Khaleel Ahmad Opposite Party :- State of U.P. Counsel for Revisionist :- Ajay Kumar Mishra,Vinod Kumar Shukla Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J. 1. List revised.
texts.facts: 4. The revisionist was a milkman and on 22.6.2001 at 9 a.m. was stopped by the Food Inspector and asked about the milk to which he disclosed that the same is for public sale for human consumption and was carrying three cans of mixed milk of buffalo and cow being 30 litre. The license was asked on which he refused. On suspicion of the same being adulterated, the milk was homogenized and 750 ml. was purchased, proceedings were done, the sample was sealed and then sent to food analyst for it's test. The public analyst vide his report dated 20.7.2001 stated of the sample to be containing milt fat 4.5% and milk solids not fat to be 4.0 % and opined that the milk solids not fat was less by 53 %. The proceedings were initiated against the revisionist on which the trial took place and he was convicted and sentenced by the trial court as stated above. The present revision has thus been filed against the said judgement and orders before this Court.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that the revisionist has been falsely implicated in the present case. It is submitted that the revisionist has denied being a seller of milk and doing the said work. He further submitted that even the revisionist submitted that there are many other persons in the village by the name of Khaleel and the revisionist has been implicated falsely on mis-identity. It is further submitted that even the report of the public analyst goes to show that the sample was only deficient for milk solids not fat whereas the milk fat was found to be as per the prescribed standard and there was no other extraneous material present in the sample which would have made the same to be unfit for human consumption, injuries or noxious. It is submitted that the courts failed to consider the said aspects and have illegally convicted the revisionist. It is submitted that the revisionist has been convicted for rigorous imprisonment for a term of seven months with fine and default punishment being simple imprisonment. As a matter of fact the revisionist has gone about six months of imprisonment out of the imprisonment of seven months as awarded to him. It is further submitted that the revisionist was on bail during trial which was not misused by him and further after grant of bail to him in the present revision vide order dated 1.2.2013 he has not misused the said liberty. It is further argued that the revisionist is aged about 53 years as of now as he has given his age as 40 years in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. which was recorded on 31.3.2011. It is submitted that as such looking to the period of incarceration and the sentence as awarded since the revisionist has already undergone the minimum sentence as per the Act, the sentence be reduced to the period already undergone by him. It is contended by learned counsel for the revisionist that the revisionist was on bail during trial and he has not misused the liberty of bail. It is further contended that the revision is not likely to be heard in near future and the revisionist has already undergone about six months of imprisonment. 8. The Apex Court in the case of Nand Lal Vs. State of Uttarakhand : (2010) 4 SCC 562 has held that the valid grounds for reduction of the sentence are the delay in proceedings and age of the accused.
